claims.text: The proposed framework couples DFT-based electronic-structure calculations with temperature-dependent anharmonic molecular-dynamics simulations.
The framework will reliably separate lattice and electronic thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The framework will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 30–50% relative to Debye-temperature-based estimates.
The claimed performance applies from 50 K to 1200 K.
The claimed performance applies to both oxygen-free and oxygen-contaminated HfNbTaTiZr samples.
DFT calculations will determine electronic band structure and electron-scattering rates.
Anharmonic molecular-dynamics simulations will provide phonon lifetimes and an expanded vibrational spectrum.
Local atomic motifs, defect sites, and oxygen interstitials modify phonon dispersion.
Local atomic motifs, defect sites, and oxygen interstitials modify electron-scattering dynamics.
The DFT component can compute electronic scattering channels independently of lattice transport.
The molecular-dynamics component accurately captures anharmonic phonon-scattering processes.
Using the derived vibrational spectra in an expanded Debye-like treatment will decouple lattice transport from electronic transport.
Oxygen-modified atomic environments act as selective scattering centers.
Oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than oxygen-free HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen contamination will not significantly affect the electronic contribution to thermal conductivity.
Earlier analytical and DFT-based estimates rely on idealized, defect-free Debye-temperature approaches.
Earlier simplified approaches do not capture the full atomic-scale complexity introduced by defects and oxygen.
The model is applicable only to oxygen concentrations within the experimentally observed range.
Error propagation, molecular-dynamics calibration, and finite simulation-cell sizes may affect the absolute predictions.
The predicted decoupling trend should remain observable despite the identified quantitative uncertainties.
